key_contribution: CDSFusion: first system integrating RGBD-VIO + semantic segmentation + dense 3D reconstruction in real time on CPU; depth-augmented FAST-feature VINS-Mono VIO module for faster tracking without accuracy loss
limitations_stated: VIO sensitive to fast camera motion; map accuracy not addressed (only completeness); not yet run onboard a UAV
reviewer_notes: VIO modified (depth-augmented VINS-Mono + FAST features) so T1 passes; framed explicitly as UAV navigation application so T2 passes, though all validation is handheld/wheeled and aerial onboard is future work. System-integration paper (C6). r6=1 for RGBD depth (auxiliary modality beyond plain cam+IMU).

authors_year: Zhang X., Cui Y., Ren Y., Duan G., Zhang H. (2024)
country_institution: China (Remote Sensing / MDPI; institution not explicitly extracted)
vio_architecture: Loop-closure-detection module integrated into VINS-Mono and ORB-SLAM3 (optimization-based VINS)
fusion_method: Tightly-coupled optimization VINS (host systems); LCD adds pose-graph corrections
visual_frontend: Feature extraction from keyframes; Colmap pose estimation; Instant-NGP NeRF virtual-view rendering for candidate expansion
features_representation: Bag-of-Words vectors with TF-IDF and synonym-similarity weighting; point features
adaptive_online: Yes - dynamically adjusted weights for candidate frames; adapted virtual-image filtering and comprehensive scoring
uav_platform: EuRoC micro-UAV dataset; targeted at small UAVs
evaluation_metrics: Loop-closure detection rate/success; APE (max/min/mean/RMSE) via EVO tool; runtime
challenging_conditions: Insufficient image texture, limited viewpoints, image blur, illumination/exposure variation, high aircraft speed
key_contribution: NeRF-based BoW loop-closure detection that renders virtual viewpoints along the flight trajectory to expand loop candidates, detecting >48% more accurate loops and reducing navigation positioning error by >46% when applied to VINS-Mono and ORB-SLAM3
limitations_stated: NeRF rendering cost (~600 ms) and onboard small-UAV compute constraints; reliance on Colmap/Instant-NGP pre-processing
reviewer_notes: Front-end/loop-closure method (C7) improving VINS back-end accuracy; algorithmic contribution to VINS pipeline. Aerial via EuRoC and explicit small-UAV target. Adaptive dynamic weighting -> r2=1. Real-time questionable (600ms NeRF) but runtime reported and pipeline targeted onboard -> r3=1.

authors_year: Hao Y., He M., Liu Y., Liu J., Meng Z. (2023)
country_institution: Meituan UAV Lab, Beijing, China (and affiliated institutions)
vio_architecture: Optimization-based sliding-window keyframe Range-Visual-Inertial Odometry (RVIO) with global pose-graph optimization layer
fusion_method: Tightly-coupled nonlinear optimization (IMU pre-integration + visual reprojection + 1D LRF range residuals); global pose-graph fusion of RVIO + image-registration global measurements
visual_frontend: Feature tracking in sliding window; CNN-based (NetVLAD-style + SuperPoint/SuperGlue cited) coarse-to-fine image registration to satellite imagery
features_representation: Point features (sliding-window landmarks); range-associated feature depths via LRF projection
imu_preintegration: Yes (IMU pre-integration between successive frames in sliding window)
adaptive_online: Yes - adaptive weight assignment for global position measurements based on online quality evaluation of image-registration localization
uav_platform: UAV (synthetic AirSim flights + real-world UAV flights with GNSS receiver as ground truth)
evaluation_metrics: RMSE of ATE (synthetic and real-world tables); drift analysis; trajectory comparison
challenging_conditions: GNSS-denied; constant-velocity (unobservable scale); season/lighting differences between satellite and UAV imagery; no prior initial position
key_contribution: Optimization-based RVIO using 1D LRF to suppress scale drift, combined with coarse-to-fine CNN image-registration geo-localization and an adaptive quality-weighted global pose-graph optimization, achieving global drift-free UAV localization in GNSS-denied environments
limitations_stated: Effective for flight distances of tens to hundreds of meters; image-registration may degrade at higher/lower altitudes; depends on satellite-map availability/quality
reviewer_notes: Range-VIO + auxiliary modality fusion (LRF range, satellite image registration) -> C5; r6=1 (LRF rangefinder). Strong adaptive weighting component (r2=1) and GNSS-denied focus (r1=1). r3=0: no explicit onboard/embedded real-time deployment claim. Optimization-based, not EKF -> r4=0.

authors_year: Lee J.-C., Chen C.-C., Shen C.-T., Lai Y.-C. (2022)
vio_architecture: Filter-based (IEKF) VIO core (ROVIO) augmented by an outer EKF for landmark-based scale correction and drift reduction
fusion_method: Extended Kalman Filter fusing ROVIO output and landmark-based visual odometry; least-squares scale-correction estimation; IMU integration in time-update
visual_frontend: ROVIO patch-feature tracking (photometric IEKF); ArUco/artificial landmark detection
features_representation: ROVIO multilevel patch features; known artificial landmark (fiducial) for absolute reference
imu_preintegration: IMU used in EKF time-update/integration (ROVIO is IEKF-based, not pre-integration; preintegration not the mechanism)
adaptive_online: Yes - online scale-correction estimation via least squares updated when landmark detected at takeoff/landing
uav_platform: Self-developed VTOL UAV with visual-inertial sensor; ground tests + real flight tests
benchmark_dataset: Self-collected ground and flight-test data (RTK/motion-capture ground truth); ADVIO/TUM cited for VIO comparison
evaluation_metrics: RMSE of position; final estimated location vs ground truth; per-case error tables
challenging_conditions: GPS-denied; VIO scale ambiguity and long-term drift; low-cost devices; takeoff/landing phases
key_contribution: Landmark-assisted EKF method that estimates and corrects VIO (ROVIO) scale via least squares using a known artificial landmark, reducing long-term drift for VTOL UAVs in GPS-denied environments without external GPS
limitations_stated: Cannot fully eliminate long-term drift or momentary external forces; requires full 3-axis motion to estimate scale; needs more experiment designs and external-force/pose modeling
reviewer_notes: Online scale calibration/correction of VIO -> C2 core; EKF-based fusion -> r4=1; GPS-denied -> r1=1; real flight + RMSE -> T3 and r3=1. Landmark is a visual fiducial, not an auxiliary non-visual sensor, so r6=0; front-end emphasis is on scale correction not feature method so r5=0.

authors_year: Kuhne J., Magno M., Benini L., 2025
country_institution: ETH Zurich, Switzerland; University of Bologna, Italy
vio_architecture: Feature-based monocular VIO (modified VINS-Mono): feature tracker replaced by on-sensor optical-flow front-end; sliding-window optimization back-end with pose graph + loop closure
fusion_method: Tightly-coupled visual-inertial optimization (VINS-Mono estimator) with IMU preintegration; loop closure via pose graph
visual_frontend: On-sensor hardware-accelerated optical flow (VD56G3 ASIC): FAST corners + BRIEF descriptors, Hamming-distance matching; CPU recomputes descriptors for relocalization
features_representation: FAST corners / BRIEF descriptors; optical-flow vectors concatenated into feature tracks (150 longest tracks retained)
adaptive_online: Not stated (no adaptive estimator; BRIEF target tunes cornerness threshold but not an online adaptation of the estimator)
uav_platform: Targeted at resource-constrained / nano UAVs; sensor module on Raspberry Pi CM4 (ARM Cortex-A72), evaluated with VICON in 4x4 m space (not on flying drone)
benchmark_dataset: Custom self-collected VIO dataset (image+IMU+OF) with VICON ground truth; open-sourced
evaluation_metrics: 3D-RMSE (sim(3) and pose-yaw alignment), translation/rotation drift vs subtrajectory length, latency (ms), compute load, power (W)
challenging_conditions: Resource/power constraints; varying camera orientations; reduced frame rate; GPS-denied indoor (motivation)
key_contribution: Hardware-software codesign replacing VINS-Mono optical-flow feature tracking with an on-sensor OF ASIC, giving 49.4% latency and 53.7% compute-load reduction (20->50 FPS) with preserved/improved accuracy on embedded UAV hardware
limitations_stated: OF sensor does not expose descriptors (forces recalculation for loop closure); high BRIEF target degrades outlier rejection / accuracy; tested in 4x4 m VICON room, not in actual flight; RMSE reproducibility variance
reviewer_notes: Front-end/feature-tracking acceleration for embedded UAV VIO; prior labeled C4 but it is not a survey/benchmark - reclassified C7. r2=0 (no online estimator adaptation).

authors_year: Wang X., Zhang Z., Li L., 2025
vio_architecture: MVS-VIO: tightly-coupled dense monocular VIO; real-time pose estimation + global TSDF reconstruction; deep-photometric-error bundle adjustment with delayed marginalization
fusion_method: Tightly-coupled optimization (BA) fusing IMU preintegration with deep photometric/depth constraints; delayed marginalization to keep dense depth usable in back-end
visual_frontend: Direct/dense photometric (deep) front-end; LW-MVSNET lightweight multi-view depth network (3 views, 68 depth hypotheses)
features_representation: Dense depth maps / TSDF volume; uncertainty mask to reject inaccurate depth (not sparse points)
imu_preintegration: IMU preintegration used (Forster et al. on-manifold preintegration referenced); tightly-coupled with visual BA
adaptive_online: Adaptive View Aggregation (AVA) and Adaptive Depth Hypotheses (ADH) modules with uncertainty mask reject inaccurate depth estimates at runtime
uav_platform: Targeted at UAVs/autonomous driving/AR; evaluated on datasets (no physical UAV flight)
benchmark_dataset: EuRoC (11 sequences, aerial MAV), TUM-RGBD, Replica (training)
evaluation_metrics: Absolute Trajectory Error (ATE, avg 0.066 m), depth estimation accuracy, runtime/FPS (10.08 FPS), ablations
challenging_conditions: Monocular scale drift, scale inconsistency, difficult EuRoC sequences (e.g., MH_05), real-time dense reconstruction
key_contribution: Lightweight MVS depth network (AVA/ADH) tightly coupled into dense monocular VIO via deep photometric BA + delayed marginalization, achieving SOTA dense-monocular ATE in real time
limitations_stated: Only a VIO (no global BA / loop closure); not effective in large-scale/long-duration scenarios; dense map memory burden grows with map size
reviewer_notes: Genuine dense-VIO estimator advance with adaptive depth modules; EuRoC = aerial. Prior C6 too low - this is C1 (general VIO estimator advance) with adaptive elements. GPU (RTX2080) eval, not onboard, but real-time -> r3=1.

authors_year: Hu J., Lang X., Zhang F., Mao Y., Huang G., 2024
country_institution: Meituan UAV, Beijing, China; University of Delaware, USA
vio_architecture: SRI-GVINS: tightly-coupled GNSS-Visual-Inertial navigation in a square-root inverse sliding-window filter (SRI-SWF) framework
fusion_method: Filter-based (square-root inverse SWF) tightly-coupled fusion of camera, IMU and raw GNSS (pseudorange, Doppler, single-differenced pseudorange, double-differenced carrier phase); filter-based reference-frame initialization; online GNSS-IMU extrinsic calibration
visual_frontend: VINS-style visual front-end (feature tracking; inverse-depth parameterization, RANSAC) - inherited VIO front-end
features_representation: SLAM features in state vector with inverse-depth parameterization; IMU pose clones in sliding window
imu_preintegration: IMU integration/preintegration used; IMU integration used to update state with delayed/asynchronous GNSS
adaptive_online: Online GNSS-IMU extrinsic calibration; sequential/adaptive filter-based initialization of reference-frame transform
uav_platform: UAV (own real-world UAV platform: two downward cameras 20Hz, IMU 250Hz, Unicore UM982 GNSS 5Hz; RTK-INS ground truth)
benchmark_dataset: Own collected outdoor UAV datasets (10 seqs, 4-12 m/s) + public datasets
evaluation_metrics: RMSE of translation and body velocity; position error plots; CPU usage and run time
challenging_conditions: GNSS intermittency/inaccuracy, VIO drift, numerical stability (single precision), extrinsic parameter degradation
key_contribution: First deep fusion of raw GNSS pseudorange/Doppler/single-differenced/double-differenced carrier phase with visual-inertial data in a square-root inverse SWF, with filter-based init and online GNSS-IMU extrinsic calibration; suppresses VIO drift in real time, outperforming GVINS/InGVIO
limitations_stated: Future work: LAMBDA for double-differenced ambiguity, observability analysis for degenerate motions, improved initialization
reviewer_notes: GNSS-VIO aux-modality fusion (C5) but with strong filter-based estimator + adaptive online calibration; relevance maxed (6). Prior T2 uncertainty resolved - clearly validated on UAV datasets.

authors_year: Irfan M., Dalai S., Trslic P., Riordan J., Dooly G., 2025
country_institution: University of Limerick, Ireland; University of the West of Scotland, UK
vio_architecture: LSAF: hierarchical multi-sensor fusion combining SLAM/odometry with an MSCKF (multi-state constraint Kalman filter) state estimator, augmented by LSTM-predicted adaptive fusion weights
fusion_method: Filter-based MSCKF with LSTM-derived self-adaptive sensor-fusion weights integrated into an optimization-based odometry pipeline; fuses stereo camera, IMU, 2x 3D LiDAR, GPS-RTK
visual_frontend: Stereo-camera visual front-end (DJI front stereo); LiDAR point-cloud measurement models; reprojection (u,v) feature model
features_representation: Visual features (camera-frame 3D points -> pixel reprojection), LiDAR 3D point clouds; state vector with position, velocity, orientation quaternion, IMU biases
imu_preintegration: IMU state propagation (accelerometer/gyro biases) within MSCKF; IMU motion model
adaptive_online: Core contribution: LSTM dynamically predicts/updates sensor fusion weights and noise covariance in real time based on sensor reliability/conditions (self-adaptive fusion, LSAF)
uav_platform: In-house integrated commercial UAV (DJI-based) with stereo camera, 2x Livox MID-360 LiDAR, IMU, GPS-RTK; also handheld/car-mounted eval datasets
benchmark_dataset: In-house UL datasets (outdoor car parking, outdoor handheld, car bridge); RTK ground truth; urban/forested/GPS-denied scenes
evaluation_metrics: RMSE / APE (max, mean, RMSE in metres), position (x,y,z) and orientation (roll,pitch,yaw) error plots; lowest RMSE e.g. 0.328/0.385 m
challenging_conditions: Illumination changes, structureless/feature-deprived environments, degraded GPS / complete GPS loss (GPS-denied), high-speed maneuvers
key_contribution: LSTM-based self-adaptive fusion (LSAF) that integrates learned adaptive weights into an MSCKF for robust UAV state estimation, outperforming VINS-Fusion and FAST-LIO2 in GPS-enabled and GPS-denied conditions
limitations_stated: High computational cost / training-data needs of deep models; future work to extend to broader GPS-denied datasets (urban canyons, indoor), more modalities, real-time efficiency
reviewer_notes: Core adaptive (C2) learning-augmented covariance/weight adaptation with filter fusion; aux sensors LiDAR+GPS (r6). Eval also on non-aerial sequences but UAV is the platform/target -> T2 Y.

authors_year: Polizzi V., Hewitt R., Hidalgo-Carrio J., Delaune J., Scaramuzza D., 2022
country_institution: University of Zurich (RPG), Switzerland; NASA JPL / Caltech, USA
vio_architecture: Decentralized collaborative thermal-inertial odometry built on JPL xVIO library; EKF/MSCKF estimator extended with a collaborative multi-agent MSCKF formulation
fusion_method: Filter-based EKF/MSCKF (xVIO) with covariance-intersection (CI) fusion across agents to neglect cross-correlation; SLAM-SLAM and collaborative MSCKF-MSCKF updates; VLAD-based request/response communication
visual_frontend: Thermal-image front-end with online photometric calibration; FAST corners + ORB descriptors, Lucas-Kanade tracking; VLAD for place recognition
features_representation: FAST/ORB feature tracks; opportunistic, SLAM (inverse-depth in state), and MSCKF tracks; VLAD descriptors for keyframe database
imu_preintegration: IMU integration in xVIO EKF state propagation (IEKF/MSCKF)
adaptive_online: Online photometric calibration of thermal images (spatial+temporal) to improve feature tracking; covariance-intersection adaptively bounds fused covariance
uav_platform: Team of flying robots / drones (rotorcraft); Mars-helicopter-style aerial application; UAV0/UAV1 in Mars Yard and simulated drones
benchmark_dataset: Real-world Mars Yard thermal dataset (UAV0,UAV1) + 2 synthetic datasets (modified VI-Sensor Simulator: Castle Around / Inveraray Castle); open-sourced
evaluation_metrics: Absolute Trajectory Error (ATE [m]); up to 46.12% trajectory improvement vs individual agent; up to 89% communication reduction; update time 53 ms (~20Hz)
challenging_conditions: Darkness/low-light (thermal), GPS-denied/no infrastructure (Mars/extreme environments), limited bandwidth/memory/compute, multi-agent cross-correlation
key_contribution: Data-efficient fully-decentralized collaborative thermal-inertial odometry: online photometric thermal calibration front-end + covariance-intersection collaborative MSCKF back-end + low-bandwidth VLAD communication, improving trajectory accuracy while drastically cutting communication
limitations_stated: CI neglects cross-correlation (conservative); reliance on place-recognition matches; evaluated with two agents / limited datasets
reviewer_notes: Thermal aux-modality + collaborative filter fusion (C5) but high relevance: GPS-denied, adaptive calibration, real-time onboard-grade, EKF/MSCKF, thermal front-end. QA5=0.5 (UAV-VIO vs prior articulated but framed around collaborative/space, less direct VIO benchmarking).

authors_year: Sanlan A., Bagci H.T., Koyuncu E., 2025
venue: 2025 Integrated Communications, Navigation and Surveillance Conference (ICNS)
country_institution: Istanbul Technical University, Aerospace Research Center, Turkiye
vio_architecture: Vision-aided / visual terrain-referenced navigation: closed-loop error-state EKF VIO (INS + visual odometry) combined with a Marginalized Particle Filter (MPF) for image-matching navigation against satellite imagery
fusion_method: Closed-loop ESKF (15-state) fuses VO measurement updates with INS; open-loop Marginalized Particle Filter fuses image-matching likelihoods (Rao-Blackwellized: linear substructure via KF, nonlinear via particles)
visual_frontend: SIFT feature detection + LightGlue/FLANN matching for VO; CycleGAN domain adaptation transforms satellite reference imagery to onboard-camera modality for cross-domain feature matching; CNN-based similarity
features_representation: SIFT features / feature scans per particle; image similarity/likelihood between extracted features and transformed satellite imagery
imu_preintegration: INS dead-reckoning via IMU integration (15-state model, accel/gyro biases); error-state formulation
adaptive_online: CycleGAN-based domain adaptation (learning-augmented) to bridge UAV-camera vs satellite-image domain gap, improving matching reliability
uav_platform: UAV with roll-pitch-stabilized 3-axis gimbal camera (30 fps); drone-grade platform; real-world flight tests
benchmark_dataset: Real-world UAV flight test data + satellite reference imagery (no public dataset; 2 use-cases including winter-season views)
evaluation_metrics: Position error (1-sigma ~50 m) and velocity error plots; comparison with vs without domain adaptation (qualitative/coarse, no ATE/RMSE table)
challenging_conditions: GNSS-denied/contested areas, INS drift, cross-domain (UAV vs satellite) appearance gap, seasonal/illumination/viewpoint variation, featureless terrain
key_contribution: Vision-aided GNSS-denied UAV localization combining CycleGAN domain adaptation with a Marginalized Particle Filter to match onboard imagery to satellite reference, refining EKF-VIO/INS estimates; domain adaptation shown to improve matching reliability and trajectory stability
limitations_stated: Coarse accuracy (50 m scale); instability/velocity error when domain mismatch large (e.g., summer model on winter view); limited dataset; future work to expand dataset and fusion
reviewer_notes: Scene-/feature-matching front-end with learning-augmented (CycleGAN) domain adaptation + MPF over EKF-VIO. Borderline C2 (learning-augmented adaptive) vs C7 (scene-matching front-end); dominant contribution is cross-domain matching -> C7. Quantitative but coarse, hence reduced QA2-4.
